subject: POC: Success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments (follow-up)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Singh <anya@atlas-payments.com>, Devon Hayes <devon@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC: Success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments (follow-up)

Hi Anya / Devon,

Great to meet you both on the call earlier — thanks for walking through the payment flows and the latency-sensitive paths. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap proposed POC success criteria, the evaluation plan, ownership, and next steps so we’re aligned before we kick off.

High-level objective: validate Redwood Inference can serve your live payment-assistant routes within Atlas’ latency and cost targets while maintaining label/intent quality for routing and downstream risk checks.

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p95 <= 200 ms for 512-token request on our Dedicated config (target for real user queries).
- Throughput: support sustained 20 RPS on a single reserved instance class (we’ll quantify by instance type during setup).
- Cost: target cost <= $0.02 per 1k tokens (productionized estimate for our quantized model profile).
- Quality: >= 95% accuracy on intent classification and entity extraction on your evaluation set (we’ll use your labeled testset).
- Reliability: 99.9% successful request rate during the 2-week trial window.

Evaluation plan / artifacts needed from Atlas:
1) Labeled evaluation dataset (CSV) with representative examples and labels — sample format attached as poc_testset_sample.csv.
2) Traffic profile: average payload size, peak RPS, and percent of long-context requests (>1024 tokens).
3) Any privacy/retention constraints or redaction rules for PII, and the S3 bucket or secure upload location.

Redwood responsibilities:
- Provision a dedicated trial environment and baseline model config.
- Run scripted load tests (latency/throughput) and quality evals against your dataset.
- Deliver an evaluation report with objective KPIs and suggested optimizations (batching, quantization, KV cache).

Timeline (proposed):
- Mar 6: POC environment provisioned + engineer intro.
- Mar 7-8: Data ingestion & baseline runs.
- Mar 9-20: 2-week evaluation window (live traffic replay + load tests).
- Mar 22: Debrief & recommendation.

Ownership:
- Atlas: provide dataset, access, and a primary engineering contact (Devon suggested).
- Redwood: POC lead (Marissa) and POC engineer (to be assigned).

Next steps:
1) Confirm the success criteria above (especially latency and cost targets).
2) Confirm POC start date (we proposed Mar 6).
3) Share a secure upload for the labeled dataset (or we can accept Drive link).

I’ve attached a draft POC plan (redwood_poc_plan_v1.pdf) that has runbooks and required credentials. If that looks good, I’ll assign our engineer and lock the dates.

Thanks —

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128

Attachment: redwood_poc_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Anya Singh <anya@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devon Hayes <devon@atlas-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments (follow-up)

Thanks Jordan — this looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Throughput: the 20 RPS target is acceptable as a starting point, but for peak batch flows we may need short spikes to ~60 RPS. Can Redwood’s environment support brief bursts?
- Cost: $0.02 / 1k tokens is reasonable as a goal — we’ll want to see the cost breakdown by model variant in the report.
- Quality: we’ll provide a labeled intent/entity testset (~3k rows). I attached a small sample for format (see attached).

Privacy: we need logs to be redacted of full PANs and only store tokenized artifacts for the trial. Our security team will send a short waiver for the POC data-retention policy.

Timeline: Mar 6 start works for us, but Devon is on travel Mar 10-14. If possible, we’d like the baseline run completed before the travel window so we can do the debrief during the week of Mar 20.

Can you confirm the burst handling and the data upload path?

Best,
Anya Singh
Head of Product, Atlas Payments
anya@atlas-payments.com | +1 (212) 555-7783

Attachment: poc_testset_sample.csv (CSV, 7KB)

Looping in Ethan (POC engineer) to own the environment and test plan. Ethan — please see the criteria above; primary asks from Atlas: labeled testset, traffic profile, and data retention constraints.

Ethan, proposed internal checklist for next week:
- Mar 6: Provision Dedicated trial instance (match instance class to 20 RPS baseline).
- Mar 7: Ingest provided CSV and run initial quality evals.
- Mar 8: Run load tests including brief bursts to 60 RPS to validate capacity and autoscaling behavior.
- Mar 9-20: Capture live-replay metrics and cost estimates; run nightly regression checks against labeled set.

I’ll be primary contact for commercial/observe items; Jordan will manage the customer updates. Ethan, please confirm any additional infra requirements (VPN, S3 creds, VPC peering).

Thanks —
